description: An 18-panel EBSD composite for six conditions of a Fe–9Mn–5Al–0.3C (wt.%) low-density δ-TRIP steel plate, arranged as three stacked maps per condition: band contrast (BC) maps (a–f), kernel average misorientation (KAM) maps (a-1–f-1) and grain-boundary distribution maps (a-2–f-2). Conditions are printed in each BC map: (a) HR and (b) IQ-1050 in the top row, (c) QA-620 and (d) QA-680 in the middle row, (e) QA-740 and (f) QA-800 in the bottom row; every BC map carries a 50 µm scale bar. A single colour bar, placed between (c-1) and (d-1), spans 0 (blue) to 4 (green–yellow–red) for the KAM maps; no unit is printed. (a) shows dark elongated lamellar bands inside a lighter matrix; (a-1) renders those bands as low-misorientation blue within a green–cyan matrix, i.e. the highest local misorientation of the set, while (b-1) is blue with dark lamellae and (c-1)–(f-1) are almost uniformly dark blue. (a-2) contains broad white lamellae crossed by dense red boundaries; (b-2) is red-dominated; (e-2) and (f-2) become progressively sparser and whiter. The group links the HR/QA processing route to loss of stored misorientation and to successive change of the boundary network.

subfigures.description: Greyscale band contrast (BC) EBSD map of the HR specimen, labelled 'HR', with a 50 µm scale bar at bottom-left. Dark elongated/lamellar bands run roughly horizontally through a locally brighter, heavily indexed matrix.
KAM map of HR. A green–cyan matrix carries blue (low-misorientation) elongated bands matching the dark lamellae of (a), giving the highest overall KAM signal of the six conditions.
Grain-boundary distribution map of HR: broad white lamellar bands with dense red (block) boundaries plus cyan and green lines in the intervening regions.
BC map labelled 'IQ-1050', 50 µm scale bar. Lamellar contrast with dark bands, the matrix appearing somewhat more uniform than in (a).
KAM map of IQ-1050: predominantly dark blue with dark-blue elongated lamellar bands; overall misorientation markedly lower than (a-1).
Grain-boundary map of IQ-1050 dominated by red (block) boundaries in a dense lath network, with comparatively fewer cyan/green lines.
BC map labelled 'QA-620', 50 µm scale bar, showing a finer lath/lamellar martensitic structure without the strong dark bands of (a).
KAM map of QA-620: almost uniformly dark blue laths, only faint bright lath boundaries.
Grain-boundary map of QA-620: mixed red, cyan and green boundary lines forming a dense lath network on a white background.
BC map labelled 'QA-680', 50 µm scale bar, showing coarse lath/blocky structure with occasional dark spots.
KAM map of QA-680: nearly uniform dark blue with slight brighter mottling, no lamellar banding visible.
Grain-boundary map of QA-680: coarser network of red block boundaries with cyan/green lines, larger white (boundary-free) areas than (c-2).
BC map labelled 'QA-740', 50 µm scale bar, showing a mixed recovered/coarse structure with wavy features.
KAM map of QA-740: dark blue overall with faint slightly brighter patches, i.e. very low residual misorientation.
Grain-boundary map of QA-740: sparser boundary network consisting mostly of red lines with scattered cyan/green, large white areas.
BC map labelled 'QA-800', 50 µm scale bar, showing coarse, somewhat diffuse structure.
KAM map of QA-800: essentially uniform dark blue with a few small brighter speckles, the lowest apparent misorientation of the set.
Grain-boundary map of QA-800: very sparse thin boundaries scattered on a largely white background, indicating the lowest boundary density.

observations.observation: The figure contains 18 EBSD panels organised as six specimen conditions, each with a BC map, a KAM map (-1) and a grain-boundary distribution map (-2).
The six specimen labels printed on the BC maps are HR, IQ-1050, QA-620, QA-680, QA-740 and QA-800.
Each BC map contains a 50 µm scale bar.
A single colour bar placed in the centre of the figure between panels (c-1) and (d-1) spans 0 (blue) through green and yellow to 4 (red) for the KAM maps; no unit or axis label is printed on it.

Panel (a-1) (HR) is the only KAM map with an extended green-cyan matrix, and its vertical blue bands coincide with the dark elongated lamellae seen in the BC map (a); all other KAM maps ((b-1)–(f-1)) are nearly uniform dark blue.

In (a-2) broad white lamellar bands alternate with regions densely filled by red boundary lines, whereas in (f-2) only sparse thin boundary lines remain over a mostly white background, so the boundary-line density decreases from (a-2) through (f-2).

The caption states the boundary colours in the -2 maps are: black lines AG boundaries, blue lines high-angle packet boundaries, cyan lines low-angle packet boundaries, red lines block boundaries and green lines sub-block boundaries.

The caption identifies panel (a) as HR in which relatively more ferrite is present, and states that its higher real GND density of lath martensite gave the steel high tensile strength (1107 ± 32 MPa) with poor ductility (5.6% ± 0.4).

The citing text states that the HR condition had the highest GND density of both the BCC phases and the FCC phase, and that heating to 1050 °C largely decreased the GND density of the hot-rolled microstructure.

The citing text states that after quenching from 1050 °C the block-boundary density was higher than the AG-boundary density, the opposite of the HR condition (consistent with the red-dominated boundary map (b-2)).

The citing text states that for the QA specimens the AG boundary density increased with annealing temperature but decreased again at 800 °C, while the block boundary density decreased continuously with annealing temperature.

The citing text reports that boundaries were classified by angle as 5°–15°, 15°–45° and >45°, with a Python machine-learning model used to identify boundary types and calculate boundary densities from these EBSD maps.

measured_quantities: kernel average misorientation (KAM) on a 0–4 colour scale (unit not printed)
grain-boundary density by boundary type (AG, high-angle packet, low-angle packet, block, sub-block)
geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density (as discussed in the citing text)
unreadable_items: KAM colour bar: no unit or axis label printed (only the numeric ends 0 and 4)

black AG boundary lines in the (a-2)–(f-2) maps are not distinguishable from red block lines at the supplied resolution; blue high-angle packet lines are likewise hard to separate from cyan low-angle packet lines
no orientation colour legend, step size or indexing rate is shown for the BC maps
individual boundary-density values are not printed on any panel
